questions.q: What does the SR-5 codename stand for?
options: Sector Rotation, 5 strategies
Sector Reversal, 5-day lookback
Signal Research, 5 years
Spread Ratio, 5-sigma
questions.explain: SR-5 stands for Sector Reversal, 5-day lookback — the short-term mean-reversion effect this capstone investigates.

questions.q: What is the raw data for this capstone?
options: Intraday tick data for the S&P 500 constituents
Daily OHLCV adjusted-close data for the 11 Select Sector SPDR ETFs, SPY, and the VIX, from Stooq.com, 2007–2025
Options chain data for sector ETFs
Quarterly fundamentals for S&P 500 companies
questions.explain: The universe is daily OHLCV adjusted-close data for the 11 sector SPDRs plus SPY and VIX, sourced from Stooq.com from 2007 through 2025.

questions.q: Why does the data loader filter XLRE and XLC to data on or after their real launch dates instead of backfilling earlier history?
options: Backfilling would be slower to compute
Older CSV files for those tickers don't exist at all
Backfilling would introduce survivorship bias by giving the backtest knowledge that wasn't actually available at the time
Stooq.com does not permit historical downloads
questions.explain: XLRE and XLC didn't exist before their launch dates. Backfilling would hand the backtest knowledge it couldn't have had — a classic survivorship-bias mistake. The correct approach is a point-in-time universe.

questions.q: What does 'adjusted close' mean in this dataset?
options: The closing price rounded to the nearest cent
The closing price adjusted for dividends and splits, used for accurate return calculations
The average of the day's high and low
The price after removing outlier trades
questions.explain: Adjusted close corrects the raw closing price for dividends and stock splits so that return calculations across time are accurate.

options: As investment advice for retail traders
